headline: AI safety group Apollo Research called for independent testers to be allowed inside AI labs during training, not only before a model is released.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a clear proposal tied to a Senate testimony, but no lab has agreed to it.
importance_line: Regulators and the public could get earlier warning of risky model behaviour if labs opened training to outside testers, but labs would have to share far more than they do now and none has agreed.
summary: Crypto Briefing reports, citing Apollo Research blog posts from 30 September to 5 October 2026, that the AI safety group wants independent evaluators to have continuous access to models during training so they can catch problems such as scheming (a model hiding its real goals) as they form. Apollo's chief executive, Marius Hobbhahn, told a US Senate subcommittee in early October that independent evaluations should be mandatory.
notes: Apollo posts ran 30 Sep to 5 Oct; reported by Crypto Briefing on 6 Oct. Pool score kept.
